high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Grants License to Establish New 100% Foreign-Owned Bank in Vietnam
high.summary: This is significant for VND and capital flows. On April 22, SBV Deputy Governor Nguyen Ngoc Canh met with IBK Chairman Chang Min Young to grant the license for IBK Vietnam - the first new 100% foreign-owned bank license issued in 9 years since UOB Vietnam in 2017. Only 9 such banks currently operate in Vietnam, including 2 Korean banks (Shinhan, Woori). This development indicates SBV's openness to foreign banking capital, potentially supporting VND stability through increased foreign investment. The timing is notable as Korea has the largest financial institution presence in Vietnam. For FX traders, this signals potential capital inflows and could strengthen banking sector liquidity, though the immediate VND impact may be limited given IBK's gradual establishment timeline.

high.title: Foreign Investors Sell Nearly 5,000 Billion VND of Vietnamese Stocks in Week 20-24/4
high.summary: Major capital outflow pressure on VND as foreign investors net sold 4,816 billion VND across all exchanges during April 20-24, despite VN-Index gaining 1.99% to close at 1,853.29 points. HoSE saw the largest outflows at 4,670 billion VND. FPT was the primary selling target while HPG led buying at 209 billion VND, followed by MSN (169.8 billion) and MWG (166.9 billion). This substantial selling pressure represents significant USD demand and VND supply, potentially weighing on the currency. The continued foreign selling despite market gains suggests structural portfolio rebalancing rather than sentiment-driven selling, which could persist and maintain pressure on VND/USD rates.

high.title: Banking Sector Q1 2026 Results Update: SHB, ACB, OCB, Sacombank
high.summary: Key banking sector performance indicates healthy credit growth and profitability. SHB reported Q1 total assets of 930.9 trillion VND (+4.4% QoQ), deposits up 4.5% to 672 trillion VND, and credit growth of 2.15% to 632.8 trillion VND. Pre-tax profit reached 4.66 trillion VND (+7% YoY). CAR at 12.6%, LDR at 77% (well below 85% limit), and liquidity reserves at 17% demonstrate strong safety margins. OCB showed stronger momentum with pre-tax profit of 1.224 trillion VND (+37% YoY) and total assets reaching 344.1 trillion VND (+19% YoY). These results suggest banking sector stability supporting VND fundamentals and potential for stable lending rates, though modest credit growth may indicate cautious monetary conditions.

medium.title: Gold Ring and Bar Prices April 23/4: Further Drop of Nearly 1 Million VND/Tael
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices continued declining, with SJC and major dealers quoting 166.7-169.2 million VND/tael for gold bars (down 800,000 VND on both sides). Gold rings fell to 166.5-169 million VND/tael at SJC. The sharp correction reflects global gold price weakness and suggests reduced safe-haven demand, potentially supporting VND stability as domestic investors shift from gold to other assets.

medium.title: Techcombank Plans "Massive" Dividend: 60% in Shares, 7% in Cash
medium.summary: TCB proposes 7% cash dividend (4,960 billion VND) plus 60% stock dividend, demonstrating strong profitability and capital generation. The bank aims to maintain Tier 1 CAR above 14% while continuing above-average growth. This substantial payout could attract foreign investment and support banking sector sentiment, indirectly benefiting VND through capital inflows.

medium.title: Vingroup Issues 350 Million USD International Bonds
medium.summary: VIC issued 1,750 bonds at 200,000 USD each (total 350 million USD) listed on Vienna Stock Exchange with 5-year maturity. Simultaneously repaid 4,000 billion VND in domestic bonds. This refinancing from VND to USD reduces domestic bond market pressure while bringing foreign currency inflows, potentially supporting VND stability through improved corporate FX positioning.

medium.title: Trade Deficit of 7.9 Billion USD - What's Behind It?
medium.summary: Vietnam recorded 7.9 billion USD trade deficit through April 15, with imports rising 28.8% to 152.5 billion USD while exports grew 20.3% to 144.6 billion USD. FDI sector drove 76% of total trade value and 88% of growth. The widening deficit creates USD demand pressure on VND, though strong FDI-driven import growth suggests robust economic activity and potential future export capacity.
